entry.name: CSG Union Demo
entry.description: Two CSG primitives combined with the union operator. Visualizes A union B as a single composite solid.
entry.qfep_connection: A∪B: two solids declared one. The gentlest Boolean, and the one that hides the most — union looks like putting things next to each other, but it fuses them, the seam between them dissolved into a single skin. The chapter's opening insistence that composition is not a pile: the moment two forms join, their boundary is renegotiated, and the inside of the whole is more than the sum of the insides.

dna.default: consensus=broad, forfeit=none - both defaults are short-circuits rather than recomputations. _cut_offset() returns sphere_offset (0.3, 0.2, 0.1) by a BARE RETURN at broad, not k=1.0 multiplied through; the two are bit-identical for these floats, so the reason is not arithmetic but that the shipped vector must never travel the same code path as the derived ones, and a later edit to the scale table therefore cannot reach it. forfeit=none builds nothing beyond the single CSGCombiner3D named IntersectionRoot at y 0.7 the artifact has always built, and never runs one iteration of the volume lattice. TEN placements, every one bit-identical: ONE bare token (Boolean_Intersection r5 c5, the naked string - no rotation, no y-offset, no config - so merged_config is empty and apply_grid_config is never called at all); SEVEN exhibit_furniture#kind:plinth#size:m#mount:csg_intersection_demo mounts across the Trial_* museum maps (castelvecchio, grande, halls, sainsbury, kanazawa, thoronet, uffizi), where _mount_artifact instantiates, positions and never calls apply_grid_config; and TWO curation_station reach-paths (Corridor_Boolean_Intersection, Curation_Bay_boolean_surfaces_0) which forward exactly {"emissive": false}, a key no build path reads, so the guarded body stamps it as metadata, recomputes the signature, finds no change and returns before teardown. The entry declares no default_params, so ArtifactIdentity.stamp adds no config either. A placement that names sphere_offset directly still WINS over consensus, via _offset_explicit.
dna.was: one lens, rotating, with a Label3D reading 'A n B' and nothing else. The truth line is a QUANTITY claim - 'what both shapes agree on is always less than either alone' - and it had shipped at exactly ONE overlap, ten times, with no way to see it hold anywhere else. The artifact's own @identity already spelled out the ladder it never got ('small overlap = a sliver; full overlap = nearly a whole primitive; no overlap = nothing at all') against an export reachable only as an unnamed Vector3, and ended by naming what it lacked: 'a readout of the surviving volume as the overlap shrinks toward zero'. apply_grid_config assigned body_color and had no rebuild behind it, so the one knob it did expose could not take effect after _ready.
dna.note: consensus is a NEW word and it asks HOW MUCH OF WHAT WAS BROUGHT SURVIVES. Nothing in the corpus asks how much of its inputs an operation returns: fontana_puncture's breach is an amount but an amount of REMOVAL (how far the void has eaten, driven by radius against a fixed cube), and this is an amount of SURVIVAL - the two run opposite. The word comes from the artifact's own vocabulary, whose @identity says 'agreement', 'consensus', 'both parties', so the rungs read as degrees of agreement rather than as four positions of a sphere. Resolved as scalar multiples k of the SHIPPED sphere_offset, so |d| = 0.374 stays fixed in direction and the axis is pure magnitude, against a box half-extent of 0.4 and a sphere radius of 0.55. unanimous k=0, concentric: face distance 0.4 < r 0.55 < edge midpoint 0.566 < corner 0.693, so the survivor is A ITSELF with its twelve edges shaved and its eight corners cut, roughly 95 percent of the box - agreement costing almost nothing. broad k=1, SHIPPED, the lens. narrow k=1.9: centre (0.57, 0.38, 0.19), nearest box point (0.4, 0.38, 0.19) at 0.17, penetration 0.38 - a cap on one face. token k=2.6: centre (0.78, 0.52, 0.26), nearest box point (0.4, 0.4, 0.26) at 0.398, penetration 0.152 - a sliver at the box's edge, agreement in name only. THE LADDER STOPS SHORT OF THE VANISHING POINT on purpose: solving (0.3k - 0.4)^2 + (0.2k - 0.4)^2 = 0.55^2 puts the last surviving overlap at k = 3.03, and past it the frame measures NO RENDER so the verdict becomes a fact about the capture. The registry order is the sweep's tile order, default leftmost, which is why 'broad' is listed first; the ladder in the code runs unanimous, broad, narrow, token. forfeit is also NEW and asks WHETHER THE OBJECT WILL SAY WHAT AGREEMENT COST - the artifact's own written gap, turned into a ladder from silence to the discarded material itself. none SHIPPED: the lens alone, you are handed the consensus and never told its price. numeral: a dark plate 0.9 x 0.22 hung at y 0.25 carrying |A|, |B|, |A n B| and the two percentages, all three integrated on a deterministic 48-cubed lattice of cell centres over the union AABB - no RNG anywhere, so no seed and no reproducibility question, and all three measured by the SAME instrument on purpose, since an analytic |A| against a sampled |A n B| would make the percentages disagree with the bars beside them. gauge: three bars on a small base at x=+0.75, heights proportional to those same three volumes with the tallest normalised to 0.6 m, so the truth line stops being a sentence - the third bar is ALWAYS the shortest, because |A n B| <= min(|A|, |B|) is a fact about the operator and not about this placement. losses: the two discarded regions A - B and B - A put back as translucent ghosts exactly where they were taken from, so the frame reconstitutes A u B around the solid survivor and you see the whole of what both parties brought. losses is NOT csg_compose_workbench's atoms: atoms puts the three disjoint regions on three SEPARATE benches to argue the regions are primitive and the operators are not, while this reassembles two of them IN PLACE around the survivor to argue what THIS one operation threw away. The two axes compose with no null cell - forfeit=gauge photographed at consensus=token shows the third bar collapsed, which is the 'shrinks toward zero' sentence in a single frame.

The ladder ends at token, k=2.6, with the vanishing point at k=3.03 named in the note so the omission is visible rather than tidy. entry.name: CSG Intersection Demo
entry.description: Two CSG primitives with intersection operator. Only the overlap survives.
entry.qfep_connection: A∩B: only the overlap survives. The strictest operator — intersection keeps solely the space both solids agreed to occupy and discards everything else, so two large forms can yield a tiny sliver or nothing at all. The primitive of the joint: where two things meet is not where they touch but where they *coincide*, and this operator is the chapter's tool for finding that shared interior.

entry.description: A box with a sphere subtracted. The operator that makes cavities and openings.

dna.was: one carved box, rotating, with a Label3D reading 'A - B' and nothing else. sphere_offset is the artifact's own declared critical_parameter ('where the bite lands') and was reachable only as an unnamed Vector3; apply_grid_config assigned body_color and had no rebuild behind it, so the knob it did expose could not take effect after _ready.

The two agree on the word and the list and each resolves it against its own geometry, which is what makes them comparable rather than merely identical. workings is the axis a demonstration wants and an artwork does not: how much of the operation it is willing to show. outcome = only the answer; trace = the removed material (A intersect B) put back as a translucent ghost in the cavity it left, which is 'absence is constructive' rendered rather than asserted; operands = the uncut box and the subtracting sphere faint and in place; expression = the operands plus sphere_offset drawn as a rod between the two centres, with both terms labelled. entry.qfep_connection: A−B: the box remembers the sphere by its absence. Difference is the operator of cavities and openings — subtract one solid from another and what remains is shaped by a thing no longer there, the hollow a negative portrait of what was removed. The walk's central power: every window, every socket, every carved bowl is a subtraction, form defined by a precise act of taking-away.

entry.name: Subtraction Suite
entry.description: Three stations on one 2.88 m bench, all showing the same subtraction. ART: a Fontana cube on a white plinth, an oversized sphere taken out of it, a luminous point suspended in the hollow, nothing explained. OPERATOR: the geometrically IDENTICAL carved solid on a post in front of a slate board, with A ghosted back around it and B drawn at the void's true radius, so the operation is visible and not only its answer. CATALOGUE: a steel tray holding five decompositions of one sphere - two hemispheres, eight octants, eight wedges, a boolean bite, forty-eight tiles - each held apart in an exploded view. One axis, `breach`, reused character for character from fontana_puncture and applied to all three at once. Use #breach:.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: footprint_cells is a COUNT, not a [w,d] pair - a pair crashes the placement engine. The bench is 2.88 m of frontage (three stations at a 0.96 m pitch) by 1.00 m deep by 1.58 m tall including the captions, so three cells are occupied and a fourth is declared because a 2.88 m slab lands off-grid more often than not. Front clearance 2 is the reading distance: the three stations only argue with each other when all three are in one view, and the whole exhibit is 2.88 m wide. wall_backing is true because the operator station's slate board is a back wall of its own and wants nothing behind it.

entry.qfep_connection: F, held still and asked three times. Subtraction is the operator that makes a room out of a wall, and this bench is about what happens to the WORD for it when the institution changes. The same void is a gesture on a plinth, a term in an expression on a board, and one entry in a tray of five ways to take a thing apart - and the depth of the cut, which is a measurable ratio in the first two, stops being measurable in the third because the specimen has no corners to survive in. That is the exhibit's own dark spot made into its subject: a vocabulary looks portable until you hand it a body it was not measured against.
entry.relationships: Synthesised from [[fontana_puncture]], [[csg_difference_demo]], [[csg_compose_workbench]] and [[sphere_splitting_showcase]] - four artifacts, three of them promoted on one day and the fourth two days later, three of which arrived at the SAME word (`strike`) with the same four values in the same order, and none of which had ever been in one frame. WHAT THEY LEARNED, and what this exhibits. [[fontana_puncture]] found that `breach` is not a size knob: cube_size never moves, and the four values are the four TOPOLOGICALLY distinct states this geometry has, cut against the cube's own three critical distances (half-extent 0.5, edge-midpoint 0.707, corner 0.866, all x cube_size). It stops short of 0.866 on purpose, because past that the cube is gone and the frame measures NO RENDER, which is a fact about the capture and not about the art. It also REFUSED a taglio axis - a slash is a cut in ONE face and the sweep photographs from one fixed camera, so half the yaws would show an uncut cube - and that refusal is why this bench's only axis is spherically legible too. [[csg_difference_demo]] took `strike` character for character and then said plainly where it CANNOT follow: its sphere is 1.10 half-extents against fontana's 1.36, so the word is shared and the NUMBERS are not, and each artifact resolves the same value against its own geometry. That is the model this whole exhibit is built on. It also found, the hard way, that a CSGCombiner3D nested in another combiner is a SHAPE and not a container - its ghosts had to hang off a plain Node3D rig or the trace would be unioned back into the solid it comments on - and every combiner here is a direct child of a plain Node3D for that reason. [[csg_compose_workbench]] holds `algebra`, the corpus's only axis asking what a closed operator SET consists of, and declined `workings` on the ground that a hub's question is the set while a demo's question is the derivation - kept apart the two are comparable, merged one is redundant. That fence is why this suite shows ONE operator and not three. [[sphere_splitting_showcase]] found the one distinction in five fracture methods a STILL can carry (computed parts against latent ones, no seam against nothing but seam) and refused an `exploded` axis for two measured reasons: the real path unfreezes unseeded physics, and the fake path works on two of the five bases and does nothing on the other three - 'an axis that is a null cell for 60% of the bench is a finished-looking experiment about the 40%'. Its five bases are rebuilt here as STATIC partitions, in its own order, precisely so the tray can be exploded deterministically; that substitution is named as this exhibit's dark spot in dna.dark_spot. Kin to [[exhibit_furniture]], whose `house` axis (white_cube, wunderkammer, depot, forensic) taught this corpus that the furniture around a thing is an argument about the institution and not a mount - the plinth, the lectern and the tray here do that job without claiming the word.

dna.default: breach=opened - the strongest single reading, and a free choice because a synthesis has no shipped placements to preserve. It is also [[fontana_puncture]]'s own shipped value, so the suite's front picture and the family's front picture are the same picture: the synthesis inherits the family's default rather than a curator's. Why it is the strongest: `opened` is the only value at which all three stations are simultaneously legible as both intact and cut. At body_size 0.36 the void is 0.2448 against an edge-midpoint of 0.2546, so the cube is a thin frame around a void that has won and is still ONE object; on the board B is 0.2448 against A's half-extent of 0.1800, visibly bigger than the body it is being taken out of, which is the whole reason the operands are drawn; and on the tray the separation is 0.68 of the specimen radius, far enough that every plate is open and near enough that the 48-tile plate has not yet become a cloud with no sphere in it. `pierced` under-reads all three, `severed` costs the cube its identity (eight disconnected corner pieces), and `husk` is the limit before nothing renders.
dna.was: synthesized from fontana_puncture, csg_difference_demo, csg_compose_workbench, sphere_splitting_showcase. Nothing was refactored and no source changed; this is a new object built from scratch at bench scale rather than an instancing of the four, because three of them carry their own room and one carries its own WorldEnvironment, a stats HUD and a nine-line instruction panel addressed to a player with hands. The gap it fills is that `strike` is shared by three of these artifacts and the sharing has only ever existed as three registry notes agreeing with each other in prose. Worse for the question itself: an axis shows one value per still, so a shared word can only ever be tested by laying two separate sweeps of two separate rooms side by side and trusting that the lighting, the framing and the settle were the same. The test wanted one frame.
dna.axes_note: `breach` is REUSED CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER from [[fontana_puncture]] - same word, same four values, same order - and it is not retyped. The script holds `const FONTANA_SOURCE := preload("res://commons/primitives/fontana_puncture/fontana_puncture.gd")` and reads its `const BREACH` at load, so BOTH the vocabulary and the four ratios come from the family and cannot drift from it even if somebody edits the family. That is the slot_machine pattern. The literal @export_enum line is written out as well, because the declaration gate reads the enum and GDScript cannot build one from a const; the two cannot disagree silently, since every entry point validates against the preloaded table and anything it does not recognise leaves the bench standing where it was. `PLATES`, the tray's five bases in [[sphere_splitting_showcase]]'s shipped order, is written as a literal instead: that script extends a vector_scene_base and preloads five destructible scenes, so pulling it in for a five-element array would drag a whole test scene behind an ORDER - and an order is not a vocabulary.
dna.finding:
THE HONEST TEST, and it is the reason this artifact exists. The shared word survives at two stations as a measured ratio and at the third only as an order.

AT THE PLINTH AND AT THE BOARD it transfers perfectly, because the construction is fontana's and the ladder is SCALE-FREE. Checked arithmetically rather than assumed: at body_size 0.36 the cube's three critical distances are 0.1800, 0.2546 and 0.3118, and the four void radii are 0.1944, 0.2448, 0.2664 and 0.2880 - so pierced breaches the faces and stops, opened is still connected, severed cuts the twelve edges into eight corner pieces, and husk stops short of annihilation. The same four objects at a different size.

AT THE TRAY IT DOES NOT, and the failure is exact. A sphere has one critical distance, its radius; a partition of a sphere has none at all, because there is no connectivity left to lose - every plate is already in pieces at `pierced`. Applied as separation, d = ratio x R, the axis opens a gap of 2*d*sin(t/2) between two adjacent cells whose centroid directions differ by t, against a cell arc width of t*R, so the RELATIVE opening is 2*sin(t/2)/t x d/R. That factor is 0.9003 at t = 90 degrees, 0.9745 at 45 and 0.9886 at 30 - within ten per cent of 1 for every division on this tray - and both the gap and the width carry the same sin(v) factor away from the equator, so it holds at the poles as well. THE CONSEQUENCE: `breach` opens the 48-tile plate and the 8-wedge plate by the same fraction of themselves. It cannot distinguish the five bases, which is the one thing a catalogue exists to do. The single exception is the coarsest plate - two hemispheres separate along a diameter, t = 180 degrees, so the gap is 2*d against a part depth of R and the planar plate opens about twice as fast relative to itself as any other. Where the ladder distinguishes anything on this tray, it distinguishes the 2-part plate from the other four and nothing else.

SO: `breach` names a topological ladder that exists where the body has corners. Fontana chose a cube, and that choice is doing more work than the word does. The tray is the negative control, and it is on the bench deliberately - a synthesis that only showed the word working would have proved nothing.
dna.second_finding: The art station and the operator station are GEOMETRICALLY IDENTICAL at every value - same _carved_body call, same ratio, same 0.36 cube, same 28 x 18 sphere - and they do not look alike. What separates them is a white plinth against a slate board, fontana's matte cull-disabled red against the demo's 0.3-metallic emissive lavender, and two ghosts. Their two source artifacts have each written down, in their own registry notes, that they are 'the same cube-minus-sphere, one as art and one as demonstration'; this is the first object in which that sentence is a thing you can look at rather than a claim you have to take on trust. The exhibit's smallest and firmest result: the difference between an artwork and a demonstration is not in the object.
dna.declined:
`strike` - the family's most-shared word, carried character for character by all three CSG sources - is REFUSED, and the refusal is the design. The tray has no B to place. Two stations would answer identically, because they are the same geometry, and the third would be blank: one repeated answer and one null cell. That is [[sphere_splitting_showcase]]'s own reason for refusing `exploded` ('an axis that is a null cell for 60% of the bench is a finished-looking experiment about the 40%'), and it bites harder here, because a shared-word test is worth running only if the stations can DISAGREE. Under `breach` they do - two measured ratios and one bare order - and under `strike` they cannot.

`workings` is refused twice over. [[csg_compose_workbench]] already declined it on the ground that its sibling holds it, and that fence stands here too; worse, at workings=outcome the operator station would stop showing the operation and become a second art station, so one value of the axis would delete one of the three framings. A value that erases a station is an edit to the exhibit, not a turn of an axis.

`algebra` is refused because adding union and intersection would change the subject from what a cut IS to what the operator set is - that is the hub's question and the hub already holds it. `comparison` is refused because the tray always shows all five bases: it is one station of three, and subsetting it would make the catalogue argue with itself instead of with its neighbours.

AND THE OBVIOUS REPAIR IS REFUSED. Making the tray's specimens CUBES would hand it fontana's three critical distances, and the word would transfer perfectly to all three stations. That is fitting the exhibit to the vocabulary. The catalogue's source is five ways to break a SPHERE; the sphere is why the word fails, and the failure is the finding.
dna.dialects: A synthesis that flattens its members into examples has thrown away what they learned, so every station renders the bench-wide value in its source's own dialect with its source's own literals. THE ART CUBE takes fontana's cube_color (0.70, 0.07, 0.07), its roughness 0.85, its CULL_DISABLED so the carved inner walls are visible through the face-mouths, its 28 x 18 sphere segmentation, its depth_color glint at emission energy 2.6, and that glint is sized at 0.06 of the body because fontana's centre point is 0.03 against its 0.5 cube. THE OPERATOR SOLID takes csg_difference_demo's body_color (0.70, 0.60, 0.95) with metallic 0.3, roughness 0.5 and emission at 0.3, and its two ghosts are built by that artifact's _ghost_material term for term - alpha on the albedo, alpha transparency, culling off, unshaded, emission 0.35 - at its own alphas, 0.16 for A and 0.22 for B, in its own CUT_COLOR (1.00, 0.55, 0.35). THE TRAY takes sphere_splitting_showcase's five bases in its shipped order, planar, octree, sectored, csg, segmented, and its own division counts: 8 octants, 8 sectors, and 6 latitude x 8 longitude for the segmented plate, which is 48 cells because that is the number its own info label prints.
dna.determinism: There is no seed because there is nothing random. No randf, no noise, no _process, no timers, no physics bodies, no Area3D, no player, no collision shapes at all. Every vertex in the tray is a trigonometric function of two integer cell indices, and both cube stations resolve through one _carved_body with one ratio, so the three stations cannot disagree about the depth of the cut by construction - which is a stronger guarantee than a shared seed.
dna.still_note: Everything this artifact argues is standing geometry, resolved during _ready and then still. The difference between two values is the presence, size and separation of solids in fixed places, which is exactly what survives a shutter. The one thing a still cannot carry is the thing that made the catalogue's source worth building - the moment of impact, the ball thrown, the sphere coming apart while you watch. None of that is here and none of it should be: every cut on this bench has already happened, and the exhibit is the aftermath held at four depths.
dna.fixture_why: Empty, and deliberately. _ready builds all three stations unconditionally with nothing gated on a player, a controller, an XR rig or a map, and there is no rate, no spin and no randomness for a fixture to pin - the two jobs a fixture normally does here do not exist. No typed bool is exposed to a token either, which is the trap that cost the prompter's box a pass: the axis is a String enum and station_pitch, body_size and specimen_radius are floats.
dna.framing_why: DERIVED, NOT MEASURED - captures are serialised centrally and none was run, so this is an arithmetic prediction and should be corrected by the first sweep. The union box across all four values is the bench's own furniture, 2.88 x 1.58 x 1.00 m: the axis adds nothing outside it, because the widest thing it can produce is B's ghost at 0.288 radius on the lectern and a tray plate at 0.135 radius inside a tray half-width of 0.46. Bounding radius 1.715 m, and the rig's distance is radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with PAD = 1.9, so at framing 1.0 the visible extent is about 6.5 m against a 2.88 m subject - 44 per cent of the width, and the bench is shallow, so most of the frame would be floor. 0.62 puts the visible extent near 4.0 m and the bench at about 71 per cent of it. If the first report comes back faint, the next move is a tighter framing rather than a bigger axis, and the ceiling is typographic: the three captions are billboarded Label3D at font 26, which the capture AABB cannot see, and they are the first thing that will clip.
dna.aabb_note: A layers = 0 BoxMesh sized to the bench's own furniture (2.88 x 1.58 x 1.00, sitting on the floor) is present, and it is doing two jobs. FIRST: the four CSG bodies are baked to MeshInstance3D on the next idle frame, but a live CSGShape3D is not a MeshInstance3D and the capture AABB counts MeshInstance3D and MultiMeshInstance3D only - if a bake returns null on an early headless frame the carved solids would be invisible to the framing and the camera would fit the plinth and the tray alone. SECOND, and the reason it is there even when the bake succeeds: the furniture is IDENTICAL at all four values, so the anchor pins the camera across the sweep and no part of a bite report can be the camera moving. That is [[catapult]]'s recorded failure, where a collapsing preview mesh re-zoomed the tile and some of its measured bite was the zoom. The anchor does not overshoot: 1.58 m is the height of the captions, which are real visible content the AABB otherwise misses, and 2.88 x 1.00 is the base slab exactly.
dna.budget: About 85 MeshInstance3D at every value - 1 base, 3 at the plinth, 6 at the lectern, 74 at the tray (cabinet, tray, four rim strips, and 68 fragments: 2 hemispheres, 8 octants, 8 wedges, 48 tiles, 2 boolean parts), 1 anchor - plus 3 Label3D and about 6 bare Node3D. The count does not change with the axis. Roughly 3,400 triangles. No collision, no static bodies, nothing to grab: this bench is walked along and looked at, not handled. Two orders of magnitude under the ~3200 element budget.
dna.dark_spot: Named rather than hidden, because it is the substitution this exhibit could not avoid. The tray's five bases are REBUILT as static lat/lon partitions of a solid ball and one real boolean cut - they are not [[sphere_splitting_showcase]]'s destructibles. In the source, three of the five (planar, octree, csg) are ONE unbroken body until something hits them, and their parts are a calculation waiting on an event; that is the distinction its own `comparison` axis was built to draw, between a part that is computed and a part that was always there. Here every part exists from _ready, so the tray shows all five as latent. That is what makes a deterministic exploded view possible and it is exactly what the source refused to fake, for the right reason. So: this station is a CATALOGUE PLATE of the five bases, not a bench of five destructibles, and anyone who wants the computed/latent distinction has to go and stand in front of the source. The second dark spot is the ordinary one for this whole pass: nothing here can be cut by a player, and the four sources all stay placed.
dna.known_gap: No map places this yet, and the corpus's standing warning applies with extra force: exactly one map anywhere (Artist_Readymades) places any artifact at a non-default axis value. A bench whose entire point is holding three framings at ONE depth of cut is worth little until somebody writes subtraction_suite#breach:severed into a map and walks the row - `severed` is the value where the argument is sharpest, because the plinth's cube becomes eight disconnected corner pieces and the tray's plates do not change state at all.

dna.default: separation=coincident is a SHORT-CIRCUIT, not a recomputation. _faces() returns the face_x export UNTOUCHED at that value, and face_x's own default is the shipped pair (0.02, -0.02), so A's right face and B's left face are the literals that shipped rather than numbers a formula lands back on. Everything downstream follows from them unchanged: the band still runs b_min.x to a_max.x at 26 slivers of sw*0.9 alternating amber then blue, _b_depth() returns 0.0 so every z is the old z plus zero, and the verdict tag and the plaque body are the fallthrough arms of their match blocks, character for character. inverted takes that same fallthrough on purpose - it keeps the shipped bounds exactly and settles the contest in z instead. ZERO PLACEMENTS, and that is the honest headline: this token appears in no map_data.json anywhere in the corpus - not bare, not through exhibit_furniture, not through curation_station. Every reference to it is a reader, not a placer: tools/build_seams_gallery.py (the boolean_surfaces row of the seam table), commons/data/artifact_relations.json (three times, each 'same category and sequence' with placements_together 0), commons/artifacts/dressing_rooms/coincident_face.json (rotations, approach, footprint, clearance, footing, artifact_offset - not one key this build reads), doc/auto_research_inventory and doc/book/text_mentions. So there is nothing to preserve except the seams gallery's rendering, and the short-circuit exists for that and for honesty rather than for a placement count. A placement that names face_x directly still wins over separation.
dna.was: no declared axis, and one asserted state. The artifact's headline is that the exact boundary is a coin toss per pixel, and it had only ever drawn the coin toss - no reading of the same diagram with the boundary uncontested, so nothing in the picture could say whether the flicker is a property of Booleans or of one particular pair of numbers. Only color_a and color_b were exports. The rect bounds, the band bounds and the 26-sliver count were literals inside _ready, so there was nothing for an axis to resolve against and the promotion had to LIFT BEFORE IT COULD DERIVE - the same first move csg_compose_workbench made when its operand pair turned out to be three literals inside _build_presets. And apply_grid_config stamped set_meta('config_<k>') for every key it was handed and had NO READER ANYWHERE: the metadata was written and never consulted. That is one step worse than the sibling's knob-without-a-rebuild - it was a knob without a wire - so this promotion needed _read_metadata_overrides, the signature compare and the early return, all three.
dna.note: separation is THE GAP BETWEEN THE TWO FACES, IN UNITS OF THE FLOAT GRID, and what it argues is THAT EXACTNESS HAS A GRAIN SIZE AND THAT CROSSING IT IS TOTAL. clear: a_max.x -0.04 against b_min.x +0.04, a visible 0.08 gap, no shared face, no contest - the exact boundary CSG actually promises, and the control this diagram has never had. hairline: an 0.008 gap, the two solids all but touching and the depth order still decided cleanly, a thin dark seam and no band - the rung that turns the claim into a claim about SIZE. coincident: SHIPPED, a_max.x 0.02 and b_min.x -0.02 with the 0.04 band of 26 alternating slivers standing in the overlap. inverted: the shipped bounds with B advanced 0.004 toward the viewer, so the band goes solid blue - one step of the grid, and the answer does not degrade, it flips entirely. The ladder is deliberately NOT monotone: the failure sits in the middle of it, with order on both sides. ON THE DECLARED ORDER, since the two disagree and the disagreement is not a mistake: the @export_enum is written clear, hairline, coincident, inverted, which is the ladder as argued; the declaration above puts coincident first because apply_dna_block.py moves the export default to the leftmost tile so a sweep reads the shipped lineage first. Same four values, and the code is the thing that renders. The verdict line under the diagram and the plaque body follow the rung, because this artifact's text is half its ink and a still that kept 'z-fight: the shared face flickers' over a clean cut would be lying. THE WORD IS NEW. Nothing in the corpus asks what distance an exact answer needs in order to stay exact. The two nearest words are taken and mean something else: seam on escher_staircase and florensky_sphere (none|hairline|gap|scaffold|field) names the joint of an impossible object, and grain on six artifacts names how a solid is divided. This is the boolean_surfaces station of the bias landscape and its charge is 'bias is conserved; show the seam' - separation shows the bias is not in the flicker, it is in the threshold that decides whether there is one.
dna.declined: tiebreak (stripes | blotch | split | toss) - HOW the contest is decided, pixel by pixel - is this artifact's own headline turned into an axis, is deterministic once seeded, and its four rungs are four real policies: the shipped alternation; the seeded blotching a real coincident face actually shows; a clean rule awarding left to A and right to B, which abolishes the flicker and relocates the arbitrariness into the rule, the seam family's whole thesis; and the literal per-sliver coin toss. It is REFUSED ON ARITHMETIC. Every rung changes only the band - 0.04 x 0.40 m of an 0.86 x 0.66 m plate, 2.8 per cent of the subject face and under 2 per cent of frame even at framing 0.55 - so the critic's hottest-5-per-cent window would be more than half unchanged pixels and the verdict would be a fact about the band's width. It becomes shippable the moment the plate is redrawn at a wider band, and redrawing the plate changes the shipped picture: a decision to take on its own, not to smuggle in under a promotion. Also declined: evidence (result|trace|longhand|axiom, 45 artifacts). There is no derivation here to show more or less of - this artifact does not compute an answer, it exhibits a place where the answer does not exist.
dna.fixture_why: NO FIXTURE, and the absence is checkable rather than claimed: there is not one call to randf, randi or randomize in the file, no _process, no _physics_process and nothing that reads time. Everything the axis and the default build is static emissive geometry resolved synchronously in _ready, so one frame is the whole account and a capture's settle cannot photograph this artifact half-way through anything. The seeded rungs that would have needed a seed export live in the declined tiebreak axis, not in what is shipped. _ready is ungated and builds standalone, so no dna.fixture is needed to make it render either. Label3D text is non-billboard throughout, so no plates are added and the capture AABB is the mesh extent. What IS required, and is not a pin, is dna.framing - see framing_note.
dna.framing_note: ARITHMETIC, NOT TASTE, and it is the documented wide-flat-subject trap in its purest form. The MeshInstance3D AABB is 0.86 x 0.798 x 0.031: x from the backing slab, y from the backing's bottom edge at -0.31 up to the plaque's accent strip at 0.488, z only the three centimetres of stacked slabs. Diagonal 1.174, radius 0.587, and that diagonal is set almost entirely by a subject which is effectively 2D. capture_config_sweep fits by the diagonal (radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing, FOV 34, PAD 1.9, RES 760), which at framing 1.0 puts the camera 3.65 m out where the visible frame is 2.23 m across; at the sweep's yaw 0.62 and pitch -0.26 the plate face foreshortens to 0.787 of its area and projects to about 11 per cent of frame. 0.55 brings the camera to 2.01 m and the frame to 1.23 m, and the plate face to about 36 per cent of frame - clear of the ~6 per cent dilution floor, with the whole 0.86 x 0.80 body still inside the frame. 0.45 was considered and refused: it would leave under 0.2 m of margin on a 0.80 m subject whose plaque sits at the very top of its own AABB. The AABB does not move between rungs (both rectangles stay inside the backing at every value, and inverted's z step is 4 mm), so all four variants are framed identically and no part of the measured difference is a camera moving.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config still stamps every config key into metadata exactly as before, then re-reads the four keys it understands (separation, face_x, color_a, color_b), and returns early unless a value the build actually reads has changed - and returns immediately if _ready has not built yet. The old body had no rebuild AND no reader, so this is the first version in which that metadata means anything. The teardown frees get_children() and nothing else, which is safe here because every child of this node is made by this script: the .tscn is a bare Node3D root carrying the script, with no children of its own. Zero placements pass any key, so the guard means none of them is even torn down; and because the sweep sets @export properties directly rather than calling apply_grid_config, the sweep path never enters the guard at all. ONE HONEST CONSEQUENCE of wiring the metadata up: color_a and color_b were always exports and were always stamped, and were always ignored - a placement passing either of them would now get the colour it asked for where before it got the default. That is a behaviour change, and it is safe here only because the placement count is zero and the dressing room passes rotations, approach, exit, footprint, clearance, extras, posture, footing and artifact_offset, not one of which this build reads.
dna.still_note: BITE PREDICTION, stated up front so a thin number is read correctly rather than filed as inert. Between rungs both rectangles move, all four outlines redraw, the band appears, vanishes or goes solid, and two text elements change (the verdict line under the diagram, and two of the plaque's three body lines). The pairs that set clear or hairline against coincident should bite hard: the band is 0.04 x 0.40 m of an 0.86 x 0.66 m face going from bright emissive to bare dark backing, and two vertical outlines move 0.06 m. THE PAIR AT RISK IS coincident AGAINST inverted, and it is named here rather than discovered in the verdict. That pair changes only the band's colour and the text, and the two colours are near-isoluminant: amber (1.0, 0.62, 0.18) has a Rec.709 luma of 0.669 and blue (0.3, 0.7, 1.0) of 0.637, so an alternating band and a solid blue band differ by roughly four grey levels in the luminance the verdict is measured in. Per channel the same change is enormous - red goes from a blended ~166 to 76 across the band - which is exactly the case focus_rgb exists to veto, so if that pair falls under TWIN_FOCUS it should surface in the critic's COLOUR-ONLY list and not as a twin. Read it there before concluding the rung is decoration. ONE THING THAT WILL NOT PHOTOGRAPH AS DRAWN, said so it is not mistaken for a fault: at RES 760 and framing 0.55 the frame is 1.6 mm per pixel and a sliver is 1.4 mm wide before foreshortening, so the 26 slivers are sub-pixel and the band renders as a blended amber-blue stripe rather than 26 countable bars. That is what z-fighting looks like, but nobody should expect to count slivers in the tile. If the axis comes back faint, crop-recheck before redesigning: this is random_walk_collection's pathology, a large change over a small area, not an inert axis.

entry.description: The boolean-surfaces seam. CSG promises exact cuts; subtract one solid from another and the boundary is a clean surface. But when the cut plane lands on a coincident face, the two surfaces claim the same depth and the float grid cannot say which is in front - so the renderer flickers, awarding each pixel to whichever number rounded higher this frame. The clean boolean is exact everywhere except the one place you asked it to be.

entry.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for boolean_surfaces. Bias is conserved; show the seam.

entry.name: Removal Room
entry.description: A synthesis shell, 5.35 m of it: three registers standing on one plinth, each holding the SAME single subtraction under a different account of what the cut left. gone is the survivors and nothing where the rule cut, which is what all six members of the `removal` family ship and the only account the mathematics endorses. ghost restores every removed cell as a pale full-size volume at alpha 0.16, so the operation becomes legible and the object becomes a lie about its own definition - at three of the four cuts the ghost register is exactly the original solid again. scar keeps neither the part nor its absence but a dark core at 0.22 of the cell where the cell used to be: a fact about the cutting rather than about either state. The cut underneath all three is computed once at build time and read three ways. Nothing here moves, nothing here is random, and the artifact has no per-frame code at all.
interactions: read the row left to right - gone, ghost, scar - and notice none of the three is the honest one
compare the same cut under three accounts of its own remainder
switch the cut and watch which account changes and which does not
entry.capacity: SEE that a subtraction has no preferred record: drawing nothing is true about the set and loses the operation, drawing the offcut recovers the operation and denies the definition, and drawing the wound keeps neither state
entry.qfep_connection: F is the cut: one rule, evaluated once in _run(), identical in all three registers, which is why the row is a comparison and not three drawings. E is the three accounts, and they are irreducible to each other - a ghost cannot be recovered from a scar and neither can be recovered from an empty cell, which is why the family needed a word for the choice at all. lambda is how much of what was removed the record is willing to carry. The dark spot is `gone`: it is the value every one of the six members ships, it is the value that looks like no decision at all, and it is the one that makes the operation unrecoverable from the object.

dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT THE ROOM MAKES, and no member can make it. Each of the six stands in ONE account and forgoes the other two, and none of them has ever had to say that it was choosing. Held side by side the three accounts are not a scale and not an ordering: `gone` is the only one the mathematics endorses and it destroys the operation, because a cell that was never made cannot be told from a cell that was never in the rule. `ghost` recovers the operation completely and is a lie about the object's own definition - at `cross`, `gasket` and `figure` the ghost register is EXACTLY the original solid, which is to say the picture of a Menger sponge with its removals marked is a picture of a cube. `scar` keeps neither state: it is the only account that is about the CUTTING, and it is the only one that would still be legible if you did not already know the rule. Legibility peaks at scar, fidelity peaks at gone, and recoverability peaks at ghost, and they are three different registers.

THE SECOND FINDING IS THAT THE FAMILY HAS TWO SCAR IMPLEMENTATIONS AND NOBODY HAS SAID SO. cantor_set and example_8_4_cantor_set_vr thin the SECTION and keep the removed part's LENGTH - box.size = Vector3(seg.y, thin, thin) - so the wound has the extent of the thing that went. menger_sponge and recursive_chair take 0.22 in all three dimensions - box.size = Vector3(thin, thin, thin) - so their wound loses the extent too. Both were copied 'value for value' from the same origin, both registries say so, and they are not the same rule: one draws where the part was and how big it was, the other draws only where. Each cut in this room gets the one its own member wrote, and the room is the first place the two have stood next to each other.

ONE CUT, EVALUATED ONCE. _run() fills _keep_p/_keep_s and _cut_p/_cut_s at build time and all three registers read those four arrays; the ghost register scales nothing and the scar register applies _scar_size to the same _cut_s. Nothing re-derives a cut, so no register can drift out of agreement with another.

THE GROUND IS COMPUTED RATHER THAN PICKED, and it is the one thing this room can do for the family without touching the family's recipes. The ghost mark is unshaded pale, Rec.709 luminance 0.881524, at alpha 0.16; the scar mark is matte dark at 0.091444. Against a ground of luminance g the ghost composites to 0.16*0.881524 + 0.84g, so the two marks are equidistant from their ground when 0.1410438 - 0.16g = g - 0.091444, i.e. g = 0.2004205 with |delta| = 0.1089765 either way. Every member so far has drawn both marks against whatever darkness its host map happened to supply, and dark grounds favour the pale mark by a factor that nobody has measured. C_GROUND is that grey, and all three registers get it, because giving each account the ground that suits it would have destroyed the comparison.

`tick` REFUSED, and it was the obvious second axis: it is the family's own word (cantor_set, menger_sponge, example_8_4_cantor_set_vr and the two aliases all declare it) and depth is what a fractal of subtraction has. Two facts kill it.

FIRST, TWO OF THE FOUR VALUES CANNOT TAKE A RUNG. `figure` is recursive_chair, which subdivides ONCE and then deforms; three rungs there would be three byte-identical frames, which is the example_8_4 fault - rungs that exist in the enum and cannot be built. SECOND, THE ROOM CANNOT AFFORD THE RUNGS IT COULD BUILD, and the number is scale-free. A Menger scar at rung 2 is 0.22 * CELL/9 = 0.024444 m = 3.08 px, inside the 1-3 px band law 4 exists because of, and no tightening of the framing moves it because tightening moves the whole shell with it. Depth is therefore a CONSTANT chosen per value by the pixel width of that value's finest scar, recorded in the LEVELS table in the script with the number that fixed each one.

THIS IS A REAL COST AND IT IS RECORDED AS ONE: menger_sponge ships max_iterations 2, and this room draws its cut at rung 1. `once` is a rung menger_sponge itself declares, so the room takes the family's ladder honestly rather than inventing a level - but the room is a WEAKER picture of a Menger sponge than menger_sponge is, and the reason is that it is photographing three of them.

THE SCAR MATERIAL IS LEFT LIT, on purpose, and this is the one asymmetry the room reports instead of fixing. Making it unshaded would pin it at luminance 0.091444 and make the computed-ground arithmetic exact under any light; it would also break the one property that keeps the six members photographing alike, since every one of them ships a lit scar and an unshaded ghost. The room reports the asymmetry rather than editing the family's recipe.

NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED, and this is worth stating rather than leaving blank. Both cantor_set and menger_sponge and recursive_chair needed dna.fixture build_mode=instant before any axis of theirs was visible at all, because all three grow on a clock and a still at the harness's settle catches one falling bar or a half-built chair. dna.still_note:
READ THE Z-STACK BEFORE BELIEVING ANY NUMBER OFF THIS SHEET, because four separate things in this room were standing in front of marks and all four were found by arithmetic before any capture. The sweep camera stands at yaw 0.62, so with cy = cos(0.62) = 0.813878 and sy = sin(0.62) = 0.581039 a point lands at screen-x = cy*x - sy*z, and a thing of depth d eats sy*d of horizontal daylight while a gap of width g projects to only cy*g.

(1) THE REGISTERS WERE STANDING IN EACH OTHER'S LIGHT, and this rebuilt the shell. A CELL cube projects cy*CELL + sy*CELL = 1.394917 m of screen width. At the first PITCH of 1.14 the register centres were cy*1.14 = 0.927821 m apart, so consecutive cubes OVERLAPPED by 0.467096 m - 33.5% of a register's screen width. Of the middle register's 1 m2 footprint the part hidden by its right-hand neighbour is the triangle {screen-x >= 0.230396}, area 0.230650 m2 = 23.1%, including 70% of its right-hand face. Rasterised at the sweep's own 760 px the three cubes merged into ONE CONTINUOUS BLOCK and the row stopped being a row - and note what that would have looked like on the sheet: a large subject, four legible frames, and a perfectly respectable bite number, because the fault is identical at every value of the axis. PITCH must be at least 1.394917/cy = 1.714 * CELL; it is 1.75 * CELL, which leaves 0.029370 m = 3.70 px of daylight between registers and zero occlusion.

(2) THE PILASTERS. A 0.10 m fin standing 0.93 m deep casts a screen silhouette sy*0.93 + cy*0.10 = 0.621 m wide, six times its own thickness. With its front face at +0.30 that silhouette began at screen-x 0.248906 while a FLAT register's marks reach cy*0.5 = 0.406939, so the right 0.158033 m - 19.4% of the width of `third` and of `gasket` - stood behind a pilaster. FIN_FRONT is now -0.30 and the silhouette begins at 0.845690, clear of even the DEEP registers' 0.697459.

(3) THE LINTEL. The ray from a register's top-back corner (y 1.40, z -0.5) to the camera rises 0.25708/0.78652 = 0.326857 in y per unit z, crossing the soffit at y 1.50 when z = -0.194 and the head at y 1.60 when z = +0.112. With the lintel front at +0.30 that whole interval lay inside it: a wedge 0.1664 m deep at the back plane, 0.040800 m2 = 4.1% of a register's side profile. The lintel and cornice now stop at -0.30 with the fins, where the ray is 34.6 mm under the soffit as it leaves them.

(4) THE GROUND PANEL DOES NOT REACH THE LEFT END, and this one is REPORTED rather than fixed. The wall sits 0.605 m behind the marks, which shifts its silhouette sy*0.605 = 0.351529 m to screen-right, so its left edge lands at screen-x -1.825600 while the leftmost marks reach -2.121750. The unbacked wedge is 0.092733 m2 = 9.3% of that register's footprint at the two DEEP values and 0.7 px at the two flat ones. Closing it needs 0.432 m of extra wall on the LEFT ONLY, which is a camera-shaped shell and not a shell. DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS EVERY VALUE OF THE AXIS, which for this artifact is the SHELL, because the shell is identical at all four values and encloses every register. Union box 5.41 x 1.64 x 1.145: x is SHELL_W + 2*CORNICE_OVER = 3*1.75 + 0.10 + 0.06; y runs 0 to SILL_Y+PANEL_H+LINTEL_H+CORNICE_H = 1.64; z runs from the cornice back at -0.645 to the plinth and CELL front at +0.50. THE RIG: FOV 34, PAD 1.9, dist = radius/tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing = 2.883952/0.3057307 * 1.9 * 0.55 = 9.857241 m, so the visible frame is 2*PAD*radius*framing = 6.027450 m and a 760 px still is 126.0899 px per metre.

At yaw 0.62 the projected width is 5.41*cos(0.62) + 1.145*sin(0.62) = 4.403080 + 0.665290 = 5.068370 m, which is 84.1% of the 6.027450 m frame; the projected height is 2.632 m, 43.7% of it. The registry predicted `cross` against `figure` as the closest at 1.1% of frame; measured, that pair is SECOND at 7.24% and the floor is `gasket` against `third` at 5.86% — which the prediction had ranked second, at 1.82%. dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED CLOSEST PAIR: `cross` against `figure`, at 15.7% focus and 1.1% frame. Both numbers are rasterised, not guessed - the four values were built in Python from the same constants the script uses, projected through the sweep's own camera at 760 px, and then put through artifact_dna_critic's exact currency: crop to the union subject box, neutralise each frame's own corner background, greyscale, resize 160x160, mean of |a-b| over the hottest 5%.

Three exports existed and none of them was an argument: bench_color is palette, rotation_speed is a rate and invisible to a still, preset_spacing is the declared critical_parameter and a distance. dna.note: algebra is a NEW word. Nothing in the corpus asks what a closed operator set consists of; the nearest neighbours ask about one operation's depth (fontana_puncture's breach) or its exposition (workings). triad is Godot's three CSG primitives and the three the bracelet offers. ordered adds B - A beside A - B, and that pair is the entire proof that difference is the only non-commutative operator here - which is exactly the demonstration csg_difference_demo declined to swallow into its own workings and deferred to 'a second object beside this one'. This is that object. complete adds the symmetric difference, built as a nested (A union B) combiner minus a nested (A intersect B) combiner, and labelled longhand rather than as a symbol because the label IS the claim: XOR is derivable and is not a primitive of the tool. atoms drops the operators entirely for the three disjoint regions A-B, A intersect B, B-A that every one of them is a union of - three benches again, and the identical count is the point, since the room looks like the shipped one while arguing the opposite thing. strike is reused CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER from fontana_puncture and csg_difference_demo: same word, same four values, same question. The numbers are not theirs and cannot be - fontana's sphere is 1.36 half-extents, the demo's 1.10, this bench's 1.33 (r 0.3 against a 0.225 half-extent) - so the same fraction of box_size cuts a different topology in each, which is what makes the three comparable rather than merely identical. On this artifact it does something neither sibling can: one offset drives every operator on the bench at once, so the axis puts the bench's own claim (that these are one family) under load. At centred the union is a ball with eight box corners through it, the intersection is that ball flattened on six faces, and the difference breaches all six faces so the box survives as its twelve edges - three unmistakably different solids from a single placement of B.
dna.declined: workings (outcome | trace | operands | expression), the twelve-artifact family word, genuinely FITS this artifact and is still not shipped. The sibling already holds it: csg_difference_demo's promotion is precisely how much of ONE operation is drawn, and repeating it here across up to five presets would fill the frame with translucent ghosts and say the family's existing thing five times over. The hub's question is the set, the demo's question is the derivation; kept apart the two artifacts are comparable, merged one of them is redundant. Also declined: an axis over preset_spacing, the declared critical_parameter. It is a distance, and a distance is legible as a number - it does not need a vocabulary laid over it.

dna.default: openwork=sampler, interior=none - PRESERVES all eleven placements exactly, and both defaults are short-circuits rather than recomputations. _build_openings matches on openwork and sampler falls to the `_:` branch's `front` arm, which is the shipped body verbatim: _sub_door, _sub_porthole(porthole_offset), _sub_arch(arch_offset_x), in that order, from those literals, with no scaling, no counting and no layout arithmetic anywhere in the path. The wall box short-circuits too - at run_len == wall_size.x it assigns wall_size itself rather than rebuilding a Vector3 that happens to equal it. interior=none returns from _build_interior_runs before a second run exists and never touches _build_ground, so the slab stays 5.4 x 0.04 x 4.4 at y -0.02 and the child order is WallRoot, Label3D, Ground exactly as it shipped. THE ELEVEN, counted: 2 bare tokens (Boolean_Architecture_Cavity and Color_Context_Placed, both the naked string with no rotation, no y-offset and no config keys); 7 exhibit_furniture#kind:plinth#size:m#mount:csg_architecture_cavity mounts across Trial_castelvecchio, Trial_grande, Trial_halls, Trial_kanazawa, Trial_sainsbury, Trial_thoronet_circumambulation_void and Trial_uffizi - pure export defaults, because _mount_artifact instantiates and seats the scene and never calls apply_grid_config at all; and 2 curation_station reach-paths (Corridor_Boolean_Architecture_Cavity, Curation_Bay_boolean_surfaces_0) which forward exactly {"emissive": false}, a key no build path reads. The entry declares no default_params, so ArtifactIdentity.stamp adds only artifact_lookup_name. A placement that names door_size, door_offset_x, porthole_radius, porthole_offset, arch_size, arch_top_radius or arch_offset_x still WINS: openwork chooses WHICH subtractions exist, never how big they are, so there is no fraction-of-the-export path for it to lose to and no explicit-override flag is needed.
dna.was: one wall run, one ratio, one label. The declared critical_parameter is 'wall_size against the opening sizes - the ratio of solid to void', and it had shipped exactly one value of that ratio across eleven placements; the three subtractions were literals inline in _build_wall_with_openings and the only way to move any of them was to name a raw Vector3. The @identity then said in so many words what was missing - 'a second wall to make an enclosed room the player can stand inside' - and that sentence had been sitting there unbuilt. apply_grid_config assigned wall_color and had no rebuild behind it, and since the grid delivers config through call_deferred (after _ready), the one knob it exposed could never take effect at all.
dna.note: openwork asks WHAT A WALL'S HOLES ARE, and at what density mass stops being mass. A ladder in count and kind against a 3.4 x 2.6 m face of 8.84 sq m, read as solid fraction of the front run: door = the rectangular doorway alone, 1.44 sq m void, 84 percent solid - the minimum claim, one difference and it is already architecture. sampler SHIPPED = doorway + porthole + arched window, about 75 percent solid, three unlike opening types arguing that all three are one operator. arcade = the same arch repeated on even piers and nothing else, 5 bays, 3.37 sq m, 62 percent - repetition of a single difference, and the wall becomes rhythm. screen = a 7 x 5 lattice of 0.36 m square subtractions on a 0.486 x 0.52 pitch leaving 0.126 and 0.16 m mullions, 4.54 sq m, 49 percent - past the tipping point, where the wall reads as a filter rather than as mass with holes. It stops there deliberately: thinner mullions read as NO WALL and the verdict would become a fact about the capture. The Label3D follows the rung ('wall - door = room', 'wall - 5 arches = room', 'wall - 35 cuts = room') because on this artifact the label is part of the claim. interior asks WHETHER THE SUBTRACTION HAS PRODUCED AN INSIDE - the thing one wall can demonstrate and never deliver. none SHIPPED, the single 3.4 m run. corner = two runs meeting at a right angle, shelter and a claim on space, still no inside. court = three runs open at the back, enclosure felt before it is closed. room = four runs, the first rung on which the player is INSIDE and the void is bounded, which is the sequence's payoff standing up rather than being asserted. The two axes COMPOSE - every added run carries the active openwork, so interior=room at openwork=screen is a lantern - and one rule governs the composition, the rule that makes 'room' honest: only the FRONT run is entered, so the ground-level doorway appears there and nowhere else. Windows repeat around the room; doors do not. Bay and column counts scale with run length rather than staying fixed, so what wraps the enclosure is the PITCH, and the fabric reads as one fabric. Both words are NEW and both were checked against the corpus before use. openwork is the craft term for exactly this - work defined by its openings - and the plainer names are taken: `opening` is held by agreement_gauge and five siblings for the pose two vectors are found in, `aperture` by breathing_room for how far a door stands open, and one letter between opening and openings across artifacts that share the Trial_* museum maps is the collision exhibit_vitrine's regard->guard rename exists to prevent. `interior` likewise: `plan` is room_shape_demonstrator's (pair|head|circle|panopticon|vacant) and `enclosure` is exhibit_vitrine's (box|bell|cradle|niche|open) for the case around an exhibit - and exhibit_vitrine stands in the same Trial_* maps as this wall, which is precisely where one word cannot mean two things. Nothing in the corpus asks what a wall's holes ARE, or whether an operation has produced an inside; the nearest neighbour, fontana_puncture's breach, asks how deep ONE hole has eaten.
dna.declined: strike, the family word shared character for character by fontana_puncture, csg_difference_demo and csg_compose_workbench, is NOT promoted here, and the reason is specific to this artifact rather than borrowed from its siblings. The word is technically reachable - this wall does have a sphere subtraction with an offset - and it would have to pick a favourite. Those three each have ONE B to place. This wall's B is three things at once, a box, a sphere and a box-union-cylinder, and moving any one of them across four named positions changes about 2 percent of the face while announcing itself as the artifact's structural axis. That is subtraction_suite's refusal in another key ('the tray has no B to place'); here there are three Bs and no single one of them is the strike. Also declined: an axis directly over the solid-to-void RATIO, which is this artifact's own declared critical_parameter. It is a fraction, a fraction is already legible as a number, and csg_compose_workbench declined an axis over preset_spacing for exactly that reason - openwork moves the same ratio as a CONSEQUENCE of changing what the holes ARE, which is the thing a vocabulary is actually needed for.
dna.fixture_why: NOTHING IS PINNED, and this is the only artifact of the four that needs nothing pinned: no _process, no rotation, no RNG, no deferred build. Every value of both axes is standing CSG resolved synchronously in _ready, so one frame is a complete account. What IS required is framing, and it is derived rather than measured. capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb counts MeshInstance3D only (MultiMesh as a fallback) and every part of this wall is CSG, so the measured box is the GROUND SLAB ALONE: 5.4 x 0.04 x 4.4, diagonal 6.97, against the wall's own 3.4 x 2.6 x 0.4, diagonal 4.30. 4.30 / 6.97 = 0.617, hence 0.62. Note that this lands on the same number by different arithmetic than a CSG-counting merge would give (5.4 x 2.64 x 4.4, diagonal 7.45, ratio 0.577) - the coincidence is worth recording so the next reader does not 'correct' it back. Do NOT reach for a layers=0 anchor here: the ground is walkable and part of the shipped look. THE KNOWN RISK, to correct from the first sweep: because the AABB is the flat slab, the camera aims at y -0.02 and the wall rises 2.6 m above the aim point, so at 0.62 the wall sits high in frame at roughly an eighth of its area - legible and uncropped by about six degrees of margin, but not centred. If the first sheet shows it small, the fix is a smaller framing (0.50-0.55 still clears the label at y 2.95), not a change to the geometry.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config now stamps config into metadata, re-reads it, and returns early unless a value the build actually reads has changed - and returns immediately if _ready has not built yet. The signature covers all eleven: openwork, interior, wall_color, wall_size, door_size, door_offset_x, porthole_radius, porthole_offset, arch_size, arch_top_radius, arch_offset_x. Nine placements pass no keys and two pass {"emissive": false}, which is stamped as metadata nobody reads and leaves the signature identical, so not one of the eleven is torn down. A rebuild frees only the nodes this script added, tracked in _owned, rather than every child - the grid and the curation station both attach things of their own to an artifact root after _ready. The four wall runs are SEPARATE top-level CSGCombiner3D nodes under the Node3D root, never nested: a CSGCombiner3D inside another combiner is a shape, not a container, and nesting them would union the returning runs into the front wall instead of standing them beside it.
dna.still_note: Everything both axes build is standing CSG resolved during _ready, and this artifact has no _process at all, so a single frame is a complete account of every one of the sixteen combinations. The returning runs are sized FROM the shipped ground slab - depth is (wall_size.z + 4.0) / 2 minus half the wall thickness minus a 0.1 m margin - so all four interior rungs stand wholly on it, the measured AABB is identical at every value, and one framing number serves the whole sweep. spatial_needs is deliberately left alone: corner, court and room want roughly four clear floor cells and the default does not, and the default is what every existing map places.
dna.hazard_noted: ONE PRE-EXISTING ODDITY, reported and NOT fixed here, because defaults are sacred. porthole_offset.y is 1.4 against a wall half-height of 1.3, so the sphere centre sits 0.1 m ABOVE the wall top and the shipped 'porthole' is really a scallop bitten out of the top edge - a circular segment of about 0.098 sq m, not a 0.32 m disc through the wall. This is why the sampler rung reads about 75 percent solid rather than the 74 a full disc would give. A SECOND, also untouched: the 7 plinth mounts seat a 5.4 m ground slab on a size:m plinth.

entry.description: A solid wall with three openings cut through it. Architecture as Boolean composition.
entry.qfep_connection: A wall with three openings cut clean through it — architecture reduced to its Boolean truth. The turn's demonstration that building is subtraction: a doorway is a difference, a room is a void bounded by solid, and the mass of a wall exists to be selectively removed. Standing before it you read architecture the way this chapter teaches — not as material placed, but as space composed, the cavity the real subject and the wall merely its frame.

entry.name: Boolean Burrow
entry.description: A seeded walk places eleven overlapping cutters in a rock block. The rock is a CSG difference with collision. The sphere profile makes scalloped hollows; the level profile uses upright cylinders with the same centres and radius. A section cut exposes the interior, and roof variants change overhead enclosure. The cast displays the cutter union without the stock or its collision. Reported components and cycles describe the overlap graph, not traversable routes or topological holes.

parameters.carver_profile: sphere keeps the original scalloped hollow; level uses upright cylinders with the same seeded centres and radius to provide a level floor. Graph connectivity alone does not prove body clearance.

predicted_degeneracy.basis: frame-share, and it is a LOWER BOUND — every prediction measured in this corpus under-predicted by 1.5x to 6.7x, because a flat-shaded estimate has one light, no shadow, no AO and no antialiasing. Arithmetic: from the canonical standpoint (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26) the 11x5x9 block projects roughly 56 m2 — the 11x9 top foreshortened to ~26 m2 plus two sides at ~30 m2. `broached` differs from `roofed` by ONE vertical shaft of radius 0.52 m through the top: aperture pi*r^2 = 0.85 m2, foreshortened to ~0.22 m2, i.e. 0.39% of the subject. The delta across those pixels is light stone (0.52) to dark cavity (~0.10) = 0.42. FRAME = 0.0039 * 0.42 = 0.0016.
predicted_degeneracy.what_to_do_if_it_measures_lower: STOP AND TEST THE HARNESS BEFORE THE DESIGN. Below ~0.16% the likely causes in order are (a) the shaft falling outside the crop because the seeded walk started its first carver near a far edge — read the printed seed and the carver count, (b) the top face being foreshortened past the antialiaser at this framing, (c) the roof cut failing to reach the surface because block_size.y grew. Open the PNGs and read <out>/_rejects.json before writing anything down.
predicted_degeneracy.note: This is the SMALLEST pair by design, not by accident: `overburden` was chosen precisely because how much stone stands over a hollow is the one interior property a camera OUTSIDE the object can see at all. The chapter has already measured the alternative and it fails — csg_architecture_cavity's step from one wall to a four-walled room, the rung its own source calls the first on which the player is INSIDE, registers 4.372%. If roofed<->broached returns under ~3% it is CONDITIONAL, not INERT, and must be cleared with `python tools/probe_anamorphic.py --token=boolean_burrow --axis=overburden` across all five standpoints before any verdict is recorded: five of seven historical dead verdicts in this corpus were false.
predicted_degeneracy.measured_2026_09_07: SWEPT AND RESOLVED. overburden measured 0.00% from the canonical standpoint — BELOW the 0.16% prediction, which this entry's own instruction says means test the harness before the design. probe_anamorphic did that and the axis is ANAMORPHIC, not inert: canonical 0.00%, opposite 20.28%, square-on 21.24%, from-above 36.07% (best pair skylit/ruined 63.74%), from-below 2.15%. A camera at eye level cannot see a roof. Cleared in doc/reports/anamorphic_boolean_burrow.json, which is what the critic gates on. Separately, a third spoil value `returned` was declared, swept, measured byte-identical to `rock` (0 of 577,600 px — a body drawn back inside opaque stone is invisible from every standpoint) and DROPPED. The axis is rock | cast.
predicted_degeneracy.conditional_2026_09_07: THE TWO AXES ARE CROSSED, AND THE DEGENERACY IS BY CONSTRUCTION. At spoil=cast the stock is hidden and only the removed volume is drawn, so the roof cut has nothing to act on and all four overburden frames are byte-identical. That is 6 of the sweep's 7 twin pairs and it is CONDITIONAL, not inert: overburden is only meaningful where there is stone to stand over the hollow. Read the per-pair rows grouped by VALUE PAIR, never the axis mean — a mean over 8 frames of which 4 are one picture reports an axis that half exists. The remaining twin is roofed vs broached at spoil=rock, which is the anamorphic pair cleared above (0.00% canonical, 63.74% from above). Measured at spoil=rock, the kept axis is unambiguous: rock vs cast is 100.00% of frame at every one of the four overburden values.
